Name: Ong Chun/Wangchuan/Wangkang ceremony, rituals and related practices for maintaining the sustainable connection between man and the ocean
Notes: Joint China-Malaysia nomination. UNESCO text: 'Developed in China's Minnan region between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries, the element is now centered in the coastal areas of Xiamen Bay and Quanzhou Bay, as well as in the Chinese communities in Melaka, Malaysia.'

Name: Urtiin Duu, traditional folk long song
Mongolian art of singing, Khoomei (China) vs Mongolian traditional art of Khöömei (Mongolia)
List / programme: Representative List, two separate national inscriptions
Notes: Same tradition inscribed separately by each state a year apart. Useful case for 'who defines heritage'.

Name: Mazu belief and customs
Notes: China-only inscription of a practice with temples across the Chinese diaspora. Lead for the historical-presence layer; not yet checked against UNESCO text.

Name: Nanyin
Notes: China-only inscription (Quanzhou music) also practised in Southeast Asian Chinese communities. Lead only; not yet checked against UNESCO text.

Name: Watertight-bulkhead technology of Chinese junks
Notes: Maritime technology; possible link to Maritime Silk Road framing. Lead only.

Name: Qiaopi and Yinxin Correspondence and Remittance Documents from Overseas Chinese
Notes: Letters and remittances between overseas Chinese and home villages. Directly relevant to overseas Chinese heritage. UNESCO page could not be fetched (robots); details via secondary source.

Name: UNESCO Silk Roads Project / Programme (incl. 1990-91 Maritime Route Expedition)
Notes: Sen (2023) links the 1990-91 expedition ('90 scholars from 26 countries', 21 ports) to the rise of the 'Maritime Silk Road' concept in the PRC. Key for tracking framing over time.

Name: Safeguarding World Heritage along the Silk Roads (Silk Roads transnational nomination support)
States: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, China and others
List / programme: UNESCO/Japan Funds-in-Trust, run by World Heritage Centre
Notes: Supported the corridor nominations, including Chang'an-Tianshan (2014). Shows Japan, not China, as funder of this track.

Name: World Heritage Institute of Training and Research for the Asia and the Pacific Region (WHITRAP)
Year(s): Established under UNESCO auspices (year to confirm)
Notes: Chinese-hosted UNESCO training institute serving other States Parties. Source for training and partnership data.
